newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRAGUE BOURSE SAYS TO BEGIN DERIVATIVES TRADE.
newsitem.headline: PRAGUE BOURSE SAYS TO BEGIN DERIVATIVES TRADE.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange said on Monday that the Finance Ministry had awarded it a licence to trade derivatives and that the trading would begin in the second half of 1997.
The bourse said in a statement the first instruments to be traded would be options on selected shares and index futures. It would later begin to trade interest rate futures, it said.
The bourse said the trade, the first of its kind in the Czech Republic, would complement the other services available through the exchange.
The Prague Stock Exchange's main PX50 index closed 0.8 points, or 0.14 percent, higher at 584.5 on Monday.
Earlier on Monday, the Austrian futures and options exchange said it would start offering derivatives on East European stock indices from March 20.

It said it would begin with futures and options on the Czech Traded Index, Hungarian Traded Index and the Polish Traded Index and its Central Euroepan Clearing House and Exchange (CECE) index, which includes Slovak shares.
Polish analysts said the move could lure fresh capital to Warsaw as it give would investors a chance to hedge their Polish investments.
